explanation: Use DFS colors: white means unvisited, gray means currently on the recursion path, and black means fully explored. A gray neighbor closes a directed cycle; a black neighbor need not be explored again.
timeComplexity: O(V+E) Each vertex is processed once and each edge is examined once.
spaceComplexity: O(V) auxiliary recursion depth; the supplied graph occupies O(V+E) input storage. Visited state and pending/recursive vertices are bounded by V; constructing adjacency additionally stores E edges.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/DeadlockDetection.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: Gray vertices are exactly the active DFS ancestor chain. An edge to gray completes a directed cycle. Conversely, the first DFS entering a directed cycle must encounter a gray vertex before that cycle can finish. Black vertices have already had all reachable edges checked, so skipping them is safe. Starting from each white vertex covers disconnected components.
walkthrough: For 0→1→2→0, DFS makes 0, then 1, then 2 gray. The edge 2→0 reaches gray 0, which is still an ancestor, proving a cycle and returning true.
edgeCases: All disconnected components must be considered.
Duplicate edges increment and decrement indegrees consistently.
